text:
If you can’t come up with anything, do this exercise for your Protector. I’m sure he or she can think of a few things that they do to take care of little one. They lock the door at night, or make sure little one eats, or say no to social occasions so little one can have a good night’s rest, or put the phone away when it rings at midnight. The warm fuzzy feelings will come later.

Choose one thing from the list to do. Make it specific – you will do ____ at ____ time. What is the first thing you need to do? Who can help you? It may be useful to rehearse what you will say, and debrief afterwards about how it went. If you didn’t do the thing, ask yourself what got in the way – were you afraid? Did you not know what you wanted to do? Did you not know how to do it? Were you too tired? Was something getting in the way? If you did do the thing, notice whether or not you feel better afterwards. It may be that even though you did the thing you are supposed to do to make little one safe/closeness/competent/happy, little one doesn’t actually feel safe/close/competent/happy. Only do things which are helpful.
